voice.style: Speak like a confident founder delivering a hackathon pitch: crisp, warm, rising energy, short punchy sentences, a beat of silence after each full stop. Never robotic, never shouting.

scenes.narration: Would you let an AI agent touch your treasury? Neither would we.
Public posts show what builders need. They can also hide poisoned instructions. So our rule is simple: agents propose. Humans approve.
This is AutoNEAR. It collects evidence, scores every opportunity in the open, and prepares one allowed action: a testnet deployment with a spend cap of zero. A human must approve it.

Live snapshot: {{live.total|w}} public records. Treasury tooling scores {{live.treasury.score|d}}, from {{live.treasury.breakdown.counts.demand|w}} posts by {{live.treasury.breakdown.counts.authors|w}} authors. But only {{live.treasury.breakdown.counts.sources|w}} demand sources. So AutoNEAR flags it: low confidence. It tells you when not to trust it.

{{run.roleCount|W}} roles turn evidence into a brief. Code limits their tools and the run budget. Citations must point to evidence they were given. Suspected injection text is withheld from model prompts.
Now the human gate. Wrong nonce: rejected. Changed payload: rejected. No named signer: rejected. Kill switch on: rejected. Only the exact confirmation phrase gets through.

Approval is not execution. You sign in your own wallet. AutoNEAR records a deployment only after the chain checks out: signer, account, and code hash. Wrong hash? Refused. Mocked RPC in this recording.

Underneath: registries in Rust for NEAR and Solidity for EVM. {{suites.nearContract.passed|w}} and {{suites.evmContract.passed|w}} passing tests, with fuzzing and invariants. They record approvals. They don't move funds.
AutoNEAR. Evidence in. Human approves. Chain verifies. Clone it, run the tests, and tell us which approval rule you would add.
